neighbours.label: a perception verb (hear, feel, see, smell) right after 'could' in narrative, the experiencer sensing something
fire: Standing at the window, I could hear the children laughing outside.
When she took my hand, I could feel how cold her fingers were.
From the hilltop, we could see the lights of the harbour below.
As he opened the oven, he could smell the bread burning.
Lying in the tent, I could hear wolves howling across the valley.
When he hugged me, I could feel his heart racing.
Through the thin wall, she could hear her neighbours arguing again.
Even in the dark, I could see the outline of the old barn.
quiet: Standing at the window, I could open the latch with one hand.
When she took my hand, I promised to call her every week.
From the hilltop, we could walk back to the village in an hour.
As he opened the oven, he pulled out a tray of bread.
Lying in the tent, I wondered whether the rain would stop.
I believe that the council should spend more on parks.
Through the thin wall, she could reach the fuse box easily.
Even in the dark, I could carry the bucket to the barn.

notes: Probe: 'I could hear' 0.31, 'I felt' 0.12, bare 'noticed'/'sensed'/'spotted' < 0.07, opinion 'I feel that' 0.05. Card top example is 'I could feel'.
